text:
The pedestrian’s statement is likely admissible as an excited utterance because it was made immediately after the accident while the pedestrian was visibly emotional and under the stress of the event. The note’s claim that every hearsay exception requires an identified, available declarant is incorrect—excited utterances can be admitted even if the declarant is unknown or unavailable. Thus the statement may come in for its truth despite the pedestrian’s absence at trial.
CONFIDENCE: 65
